# `start_compass_auto_calibration`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Calibrate the compass by rotating the mount automatically (firmware 9.75).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / READ |
| Side-effect tier | D |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.75, handler @0xd6cb0 (64-bit build), @0x612ec (32-bit build) |

New in firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0. Takes no parameters. Starts the compass calibration worker together with a mount rotation thread that turns the mount through a full circle in a safe direction chosen from the mount's own state. Progress and the result arrive as CompassCalibration events; in firmware 9.75 a fail event carries a code (560 to 565, see the error table). On success the calibration is stored and the guider azimuth state is cleared. If the rotation thread fails to start, the reply may carry a stale code (READ).

Side effects: Rotates the mount, samples the magnetometer, and on success stores the sensor calibration and clears the guider azimuth state.

| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"start_compass_auto_calibration"`. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 524 | a calibration or the rotation thread is already running | `busy` |
| 203 | the mount is moving | `mount moving` |
| 560 | the mount motion-state query failed | `compass communication failed` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Rotation failures after the reply surface as CompassCalibration fail events with codes 560 to 565.

## Example

Request, request - READ shape, not captured:

```json
{"id":90,"method":"start_compass_auto_calibration"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_compass_auto_calibration","result":0,"code":0,"id":90}
```
